thread:
incident-bot: 🔔 Pager: High routing spillover detected for us-east-1 at 2026-03-15T02:33:19Z. Symptom: 15% of requests routed to fallback model in eu-west-1, elevated 5xx on primary model. Severity: P2. Paging ops-oncall.
ops-oncall: on it, joining. tag me if you need escalation.
Samir: seeing this in prod routing logs — latency spike in kafka->router around 02:31 UTC, then routing policy started spilling to eu-west-1 fallback. Customers impacted: a subset of enterprise tenants pinned to gpt-xl.
Maria: which tenants? any paying customers in the EU? cc @Ben for account impact.
Samir: quick list: tenant_ids: ["acme-inc", "northbridge", "openai-partner"]. acme and northbridge had ~8% error increase. openai-partner small noise.
Aisha: hypothesis: fallback selection prefers lower-cost variants in other regions when the primary queue latency > 200ms. If the regional weight calc is wrong we'll see cross-region spillovers.
Ben: confirming billing-impact alert not firing yet, but support tickets inbound. I'll start a customer notify template if we need it. :thinking_face:
Samir: dumping a short excerpt from router logs (stripped PII):
```
2026-03-15T02:31:08Z router-1 INFO route_decision tenant=acme model=gpt-xl region=us-east-1 latency=212ms queue=4500ms action=spillover->eu-west-1 fallback_model=gpt-medium reason=latency_threshold
2026-03-15T02:31:09Z router-1 WARN model_health model=gpt-xl region=us-east-1 error_rate=0.06 5xx=0.04
2026-03-15T02:31:10Z router-2 INFO route_decision tenant=northbridge model=gpt-xl region=us-east-1 latency=198ms action=serve_primary
2026-03-15T02:31:12Z router-1 INFO cache_prefill tenant=acme key=prefix-abc hit=false action=fallback
```
Maria: interesting, acme was above 200ms but northbridge hovered under. So spillover is tenant-scoped. Could be queue accounting per-tenant.
Jules: can we get the routing policy snapshot that was active at the time? need the tier weights and latency thresholds.
Samir: pulled policy version 2026-03-08T15:00Z (active):
```
{"policy_id":"routing-v2","global_latency_threshold_ms":200,"fallback_preference":[{"score":10,"region":"eu-west-1","model":"gpt-medium"},{"score":5,"region":"us-east-2","model":"gpt-small"}],"per_tenant_overrides":{}}
```
Aisha: aha — fallback preference lists eu-west-1 first. That explains cross-region pick. If primary suffers transient queueing, policy will pick eu-west-1 by design. But why did queueing spike for acme only? maybe their concurrency pattern/long-running prompts.
Ben: do we have traces showing long-running token generation for acme sessions?
Samir: yes - here's a sample trace IDs: [trace-7a2, trace-7a3]. Stack snippet shows progressive KV lookup stalls, likely due to a node in shard-3 GC pause.
Samir: trace excerpt:
```
TRACE trace-7a2: shard=3 step=kv_get latency_ms=1200
TRACE trace-7a2: shard=3 step=queue_wait latency_ms=300
TRACE trace-7a2: model_infer latency_ms=80
```
ops-oncall: GC pause on shard-3 would explain only some tenants affected — those pinned to that shard. Can infra please check shard-3 host metrics and OOM/GCs? @deploy-bot can you pull recent host logs for shard-3?
deploy-bot: fetched logs for shard-3 (range 02:20-02:40 UTC): host-3 had a 1.1s stop-the-world GC at 02:30:59, CPU spike to 98%, memory stable.
Aisha: ok, root cause chain emerging: GC pause caused queue wait increase -> router latency threshold crossed -> routing policy spilled to eu-west-1 fallback model (gpt-medium) -> cross-region misroute and customer-visible increased errors.
Maria: mitigation options now? Can we prefer same-region fallback model instead of cross-region? Also can we temporarily bump latency threshold for affected tenants to avoid spillover?
Jules: for live mitigation I'd suggest two steps (a) patch routing policy to prefer same-region fallbacks (b) invalidate fallback_preference ordering to deprioritize eu-west-1 for us-east-1 origin. This is a small config change.
Samir: prepared a CLI patch (dry run):
```
redwoodctl routing update --policy routing-v2 --pref 'same-region-first'
```
Ben: go for patch. I'll run it and monitor.
Ben: executing patch now. rolling to us-east-1 routers.
deploy-bot: policy update deployed to routers in us-east-1 at 02:36:22 UTC, version routing-v2+patch1.
ops-oncall: monitoring metrics — initial drop in spillover count from 15%->2% in the last 3 minutes. latency on acme sessions trending down.
Samir: collecting a compact timeline for the RCA doc:
- 02:30:59 UTC host-3 GC pause (shard-3)
- 02:31:08 UTC router detected queue latency >200ms for tenant acme -> spillover to eu-west-1 fallback
- 02:31:20-02:35:00 UTC increased 5xx and cross-region traffic observed
- 02:36:22 UTC routing policy patch deployed preferring same-region fallback
- 02:38:00 UTC spillover reduced to baseline
Maria: good, can we capture per-tenant request counts & error delta for the affected window so support can triage customer comms?
Samir: per-tenant delta (02:30-02:38 UTC):
- acme-inc: requests=12.8k -> errors +960 (+7.5%)
- northbridge: requests=9.4k -> errors +120 (+1.3%)
- openai-partner: requests=3.1k -> errors +10 (+0.3%)
Jules: that should be enough for a first-pass customer impact note. Ben, can you draft a short notify for acme and northbridge?
Ben: will do, will mention transient GC and routing mitigation, avoiding technical blame. cc legal if needed.
Aisha: hypothesis for RCA: primary trigger was infra GC pause, secondary failure mode is routing policy lacking locality preference which allowed cross-region fallback leading to increased error surface and higher latencies for fallbacks. Action items: add locality-aware fallback, add per-shard GC alerts, add automated throttling on routing spillover per-tenant.
ops-oncall: handoff to next oncall in 30m. Summary for handoff: incident resolved to baseline after policy patch; root cause: host-3 GC pause; mitigations applied: routing policy patched to prefer same-region fallback; follow-ups listed in thread.
Samir: I'll attach logs and the timeline doc in the incident board. Follow-ups: 1) Add same-region fallback test to canary suite (owner: eng-runtime/Aisha). 2) GC alert thresholds + auto-restart for shard hosts (owner: eng-infra/Samir). 3) Add routing unit test for per-tenant queue accounting (owner: eng-platform/Jules). 4) Postmortem writeup (owner: ops-oncall).
Maria: thanks all. I'll coordinate customer comms and legal review. Closing note: no data exposure, impact limited to request errors/latency.
ops-oncall: handing off — next oncall please pick up the RCA doc and ensure follow-up tasks are in the cadence. :white_check_mark:
